Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Titan Aerospace Systems Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Titan Aerospace Systems' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are David Mitchell, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mark Reilly, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Alex Kim, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on our current expectations but are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

David Mitchell:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Titan Aerospace Systems delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across defense systems, commercial aerospace, and space technologies. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. Today, I will cover several key areas central to our results:

First, overall company performance highlights and key takeaways. I'm thrilled to kick off with what was another standout quarter, underscoring our leadership across the Aerospace & Defense spectrum. We delivered record consolidated revenue of $8.7 billion, up 14% year-over-year and surpassing our guidance midpoint. This marks our eighth straight quarter of double-digit growth, fueled by commercial aviation recovery and surging defense demand amid escalating geopolitical tensions. Breaking it down by segment: Defense Systems, our largest unit at 52% of revenue, posted $4.5 billion, up 18% year-over-year. Key drivers included $1.2 billion in deliveries on the Next-Generation Air Dominance or NGAD demonstrator program—analogous to the evolution of the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter—and accelerated production ramps for hypersonic boost-glide vehicles, where we're partnering with the U.S. Air Force on the ARRW follow-on. International sales here jumped 25%, with major awards from NATO allies like the UK Ministry of Defence for integrated air defense systems featuring our Gallium Nitride or GaN-based AESA radars, outperforming legacy systems from competitors like Raytheon.

Commercial Aerospace contributed $2.9 billion, up 12% year-over-year, as OEM pull-through strengthened. We're seeing Boeing 737 MAX and Airbus A320neo build rates normalizing post-supply chain issues, with our composite winglets and nacelle assemblies—certified for 15% drag reduction—capturing 28% market share in aftermarket upgrades. Business jet demand remains strong, bolstered by our collaborations on the Embraer E-Jet E2.

Space & Advanced Technologies rounded out at $1.3 billion, surging 22% year-over-year on $850 million in Space Force contracts for reusable satellite constellations and laser communications payloads. Our subsystems for New Glenn-class launch vehicles are now in full-rate production, positioning us ahead of peers like Northrop Grumman in the cislunar economy.

On profitability, adjusted operating margins expanded 210 basis points to 14.8%, our highest in five years, driven by fixed-price contract efficiencies, labor productivity gains from our Industry 4.0 digital thread initiatives, and favorable mix from high-margin indefinite delivery indefinite quantity or IDIQ task orders. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $2.85, beating consensus by $0.12 and up 22% year-over-year. Free cash flow was a stellar $1.1 billion, or 13% of revenue. Our balance sheet remains fortress-like with net debt to EBITDA at 1.8 times and $12 billion in liquidity. Funded backlog swelled to $128 billion, up 16% year-over-year, with a book-to-bill of 1.3 times—providing over three years of revenue visibility. Unfunded backlog adds another $45 billion, including options on the Army's Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft or FLRAA and hypersonic defense corridors.

Regionally, U.S. DoD and NASA exposure is our bedrock at 65% of backlog, but international diversification accelerated: EMEA grew 19% on Foreign Military Sales or FMS offsets for Patriot-like systems, APAC jumped 32% amid Taiwan Strait tensions boosting sales of our MQ-Next unmanned loyal wingman drones, and we're pursuing Middle East opportunities with directed energy weapon prototypes for counter-drone missions.

Strategically, we're leaning into megatrends with R&D investment up to 6.2% of revenue, or $540 million this quarter, targeting digital engineering twins for 30% faster program certification—like our NGAD digital fly-first approach—and sustainable tech, including hybrid-electric propulsion for NASA's X-59 QueSST successor. Supply chain resilience is paying off; we've derisked 85% of Tier 1 spend with dual-sourcing, mitigating titanium and rare earth inflation.

Challenges like inflation on labor and forgings persist, but our pricing actions and AI-optimized manufacturing lines have offset them. Geopolitical risks are actually tailwinds—global defense budgets projected at $2.4 trillion for 2024 per SIPRI, with U.S. topline up 4.5% to $886 billion.

In short, Titan is uniquely positioned at the intersection of great power competition and commercial rebound. We're shaping the future through tech leadership in hypersonics, autonomy, and space resilience.

Second, drivers of aftermarket performance, which Mark will address in more detail operationally. Third, free cash flow generation and utilization. Fourth, our capital deployment strategy. And fifth, updated revenue and earnings guidance for the full year. Lisa will provide deep dives on those financial aspects shortly.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NGAD program and its potential to drive our future growth trajectory. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily.

With that, I'll turn it over to Lisa.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $8.7 billion, representing a 14% increase year-over-year. Our earnings per share were $2.85 on an adjusted basis. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $12 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year is being raised today, as I'll detail. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Our specific financial highlights include gross margin expansion to 14.8%, operating income of $1.3 billion, up 22% year-over-year, and free cash flow of $1.8 billion in the quarter.

Let me expand on the updated full-year 2024 guidance, which we're raising based on Q3 strength, robust order intake, and favorable industry tailwinds. As a leader in integrated defense systems, next-generation aircraft, precision munitions, and space architectures—with key programs spanning the F-35 Lightning II joint strike fighter, hypersonic weapons like our HX-2 glide vehicle, and the B-21 Raider bomber family—we now guide to full-year revenue of $31.0 to $32.5 billion, up from our prior range of $29.5 to $31.0 billion. This represents about 12% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, driven by accelerated production ramps and higher-than-expected international sales. Segmentally, Aeronautics expected at $14.2 to $15.0 billion or 46% of total, Missiles and Fire Control $9.8 to $10.5 billion or 31%, Space Systems $5.5 to $6.0 billion or 18%, and Integrated Systems $1.5 billion or 5%.

Adjusted EPS guidance now $14.20 to $15.00, up from $13.50 to $14.30, implying 15% growth at midpoint, with operating margins at 13.5% to 14.0%. Free cash flow on track for $6.0 to $6.5 billion year-to-date pace, supporting repurchases and a dividend increase.

Key drivers: Book-to-bill at 1.3:1, backlog over $145 billion including $28 billion funded—wins like $4.2 billion FMS for Lot 16 F-35s to NATO allies Poland and Finland, $1.8 billion HX-2. Commercial aerostructures up 25% sequentially for Boeing 787 and Airbus A350, 737 MAX nacelles at 45 per month. Defense budgets positive: FY25 NDAA $30 billion more for air dominance, benefiting NGAD at 85% digital twin maturity. Geopolitics driving 30% precision strike growth.

Regionally: U.S. DoD 65%, F-35 Lots 17-18 margin expansion 150 bps; Europe/NATO 20%, Patriot PAC-3 up 40%, Skyborg CCA; Middle East/APAC 10%, Saudi F-15EX, Qatar MQ-9, Japan SPY-7; other 5% space like GPS IIIF.

Initiatives: Supply chain dual-sourcing titanium, AI inventory cut lead times 35%; R&D 8% on DEWs 300kW HEL, quantum comms; M&A like $850 million AeroTech Sensors for counter-UAS. Productivity 200-300 bps, Q3 margins 13.8%, Q4 14.2%, tax 19%. Risks: CR delays $500M, rare earths, engine delays—buffered by 1.25x leverage, $8 billion liquidity.

This reflects execution in a $1 trillion global A&D market growing 5-7% CAGR.

Shifting to free cash flow generation and utilization, which remains a cornerstone of our strength. In Q3, we generated $1.8 billion, year-to-date $5.2 billion, up 15-25% year-over-year, on track for full-year $6.0 to $6.5 billion midpoint. FCF—or operating cash less CapEx—shows our cash power post-growth investments, resilient to titanium volatility up 15% from Russian restrictions and labor shortages.

Pillars: Backlog conversion from $145 billion (40% international, F-35 Europe/Mideast, P-8A Indo-Pacific), 28% funded to cash vs. 25% target, F-35 Lot 15 at 156/year Fort Worth. Operating cash $2.4 billion Q3, up 30%: $450 million commercial nacelles 737 MAX/A320neo at 82% load factors; $650 million defense sustainment C-130J PBL 95% rates; $200 million Army FLRAA progress payments. Working capital: DSO 55 days via Oracle ERP 70% automated, inventory turns 4.2x despite hypersonic pre-builds.

CapEx $1.1 billion year-to-date or 4-5% sales: $250 million Huntsville additive manufacturing for 30% faster titanium; $150 million NGAD digital twins 15% sustainment savings; UK Tempest $100 million for €100 billion potential.

Utilization: 50-60% shareholder returns—$2.8 billion YTD buybacks 9.5 million shares at $285 avg retiring 2.1% float, $1.3 billion dividends up 12% to $0.85 quarterly ($3.40 annual, 2.4% yield, 45% payout, 10% 5-year CAGR); deleveraging to 1.2x EBITDA, refinanced $3 billion notes at 4.1% saving $45 million; M&A $1.9 billion Quantum Dynamics Labs for GaN RF/AI EW accretive $0.15 FY25, $250 million synergies, $3-4 billion FY25 pipeline DEWs/sats; balance CapEx/debt.

FCF margins 18%, compounding 10-12% CAGR on $50 billion new awards like Qatar F-15QA, Australia Loyal Wingman. Risks Boeing STARLINER, rare earths—mitigated 85% repeat business, FCF Factory AI for 20% CapEx efficiency.

Finally, our capital deployment strategy, a cornerstone for superior total shareholder returns while positioning for A&D leadership. Disciplined and opportunistic, aligned with returning capital, high-ROIC growth, balance sheet strength. Q3 $1.8 billion FCF, YTD $5.2 billion up 15%, from $145 billion backlog, 1.3x book-to-bill, fixed-price execution. Defense budgets $850 billion FY25 U.S. DoD plus supplements.

Shareholder returns first: Board approved 12% dividend hike to $0.85 quarterly, 28th annual increase, $3.40 annual 2.4% yield, 45% payout, 10% 5-year CAGR outpacing peers. Repurchases: $4.5 billion authorized, Q3 4.2 million shares $1.2 billion at $285 (18x forward EPS), YTD $2.8 billion 9.5 million shares 2.1% float, 5 cents Q3 EPS accretion, ROIC to 16%. TSR 28% YTD, +12 S&P A&D.

Growth investments: M&A in hypersonics/autonomy/contested logistics—NGAD/CCA/Replicator. $1.9 billion Quantum Dynamics Labs August close: GaN RF/AI EW for F-35 Block 4 APG-89, accretive $0.15 FY25, $250 million synergies, bolsters $12 billion EW, Middle East F-35 $2.5 billion offsets Israel/UAE ITAR. FY25 $3-4 billion M&A from $12 billion cash/$5 billion revolver: $800 million DEWs like Raytheon HELIOS, European smallsat for NATO $10 billion space awareness. Hurdles: 12%+ IRR, 2x ROIC 3 years, strategic fit 8/10. Integrate via Huntsville/Palmdale Tech Fusion Centers, IR&D to 4.2%.

CapEx $1.1 billion FY24 up 8% Fort Worth B-21 composites; leverage 1.2x, $7.2 billion cash 18 months runway, refinanced $3 billion 4.1% saving $45 million.

Flywheel: 50-60% returns, 25-30% M&A, balance CapEx/debt—350 bps ROIC expansion since 2020, capturing $20 billion hypersonic/MQ-Next/AUKUS. Hedged: 55% U.S. DoD, 25% international FMS Poland FA-50/ABMS, 20% commercial 15% margins. Confident 8-10% revenue, 12-15% EPS CAGR.

Gross margin 14.8%, operating income $1.3 billion, free cash flow $1.8 billion Q3 as noted.

I'll now pass to Mark for operational updates.

Mark Reilly:
Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in our supply chain management, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like F-35 Lot 15 at 156 aircraft annually and B-21 low-rate initial production. We are also investing in automation and digital technologies to improve efficiency and reduce costs. Specifically, let me dive into the drivers of our aftermarket performance, which delivered $2.8 billion in Q3 revenues, up 18% year-over-year and 42% of total top-line, with adjusted EBITDA margins at 32.5%, up 210 basis points. This highlights the high-margin, annuity-like nature of our services, fueled by fleet utilization, accelerating maintenance cycles, and digital transformation.

Fleet utilization is the largest tailwind. Global commercial air traffic surpassed pre-pandemic with IATA ASKs up 12% YTD. Our GAD-900 series engines on 65% commercial aftermarket averaged 13.2 daily hours, up 22% YoY above 11-hour model; single-aisle LCCs like Ryanair/IndiGo over 14 hours on LEAP-X derivatives.

Defense utilization compelling from Middle East/Eastern Europe ops: F-35A/B/C 1.2 million hours Q3 up 15%, extended patrols/NATO; F-15EX Middle East 25% above average, $450 million or 16% segment.

High utilization boosts MRO/spares: shop visits 1,450 up 24%, large visits 30%; pricing mid-single digits under TotalCare/Eagle Plans covering 72% base.

Maintenance cycles compressing: Commercial TBO 22,000 cycles from 25,000, 737 MAX/A320neo 55% aftermarket in C/D-checks up 28%, San Antonio 40% more A320neo nacelles.

Defense: F-35 Block 4 thermal systems unscheduled on 15% fleet $320 million; FCAS Rafale/Eurofighter PBL 60% share; Asia-Pacific Typhoon/Su-30MKI 20% ramp $280 million Singapore hub.

Technical initiatives: GAD Sentinel predictive analytics/digital twins/AI/ML on 15 petabytes data optimize intervals, cut no-fault-found 35%, on-wing 99.7% LEAP-X, MTBUR 28,000 hours; Delta/United extensions lock 85% 2025. Supply chain 98% availability vs. 92% industry.

Installed base up 8% to 28,000 units, defense 45% from 38% via $12 billion F-35 IDIQ, Australia Loyal Wingman. Target 15-20% CAGR to 2028 bundling with hypersonics. Risks ASK/fuel/DoD sequestration mitigated by 4.2x book-to-bill, $45 billion backlog 70% aftermarket. Full-year $10.5-11 billion, 31-33% margins. Confident in 20% organic growth.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Josh Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Josh Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the capital deployment strategy, particularly the M&A pipeline?

David Mitchell:
Certainly, Josh. As Lisa detailed, our approach is balanced and disciplined—prioritizing shareholder returns with the recent 12% dividend increase and aggressive buybacks, while opportunistically pursuing tuck-in M&A like the Quantum Dynamics Labs deal that enhances our EW capabilities for F-35 and international exports. We've got $3-4 billion earmarked for FY25 targeting hypersonics and DEWs with strict ROIC hurdles, all while maintaining our fortress balance sheet. This flywheel supports sustained growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about the updated revenue and earnings guidance for the full year—what's giving you confidence in the raised midpoint?

Lisa Chen:
Emily, great question. The uplift comes from our 1.3x book-to-bill and $145 billion backlog visibility, accelerated ramps in F-35 and commercial aerostructures, plus geopolitical tailwinds like NDAA increments and international FMS wins. Margins are benefiting from productivity and favorable mix, with risks well-buffered by liquidity. We're executing in a growing market.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Regarding the drivers of aftermarket performance, how sustainable is the fleet utilization uplift?

Dr. Alex Kim:
Raj, thanks. Mark covered the dynamics well, but from a tech perspective, our GAD Sentinel platform with AI/ML and digital twins on vast fleet data is extending reliability to 99.7% and optimizing cycles, locking in multi-year contracts. Defense tempos from NGAD sustainment and regional ops, combined with commercial recovery, make this highly sustainable, targeting 15-20% CAGR.

David Mitchell:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 2024 earnings call. A replay will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
